title: Rolling SLI Census & Degradation Credit Orchestrator for Per-Endpoint Model Contracts
creator: Priya Natarajan
description: Goal: Implement a rolling SLI census and a degradation-credit orchestrator that automates error-budget allocation and temporary crediting across endpoints and model variants during multi-region failover and circuit-breaker-driven load-shedding. This ticket defines the API surface, telemetry requirements, decision heuristics, and integration points with Console, routing layer, and rollout guardrails. We aim to reduce manual rescue operations during regional pressure by enabling programmatic redistribution of degradation allowance while preserving service contracts for high-priority routes.
background: We frequently see transient regional capacity pressure where regional failover plus variant preemption causes churn in per-endpoint SLIs. Current manual reallocation (pager, runbook) is slow and leads to noisy falls-through to lower-quality variants. The rolling SLI census provides a consistent snapshot of weighted request quality and burn rates per endpoint/model/region, and the orchestrator uses that to grant short-lived degradation credits or trigger graceful circuit actions.
acceptance_criteria: Rolling census process captures per-endpoint SLIs (p50/p95 latency, availability, response-quality score) every 1 minute and stores 12-hour sliding window metrics.
Orchestrator can auto-assign 'degradation credits' to an endpoint for up to 10 minutes based on configured rules and available error budget pool.
Integration with routing layer to attach credit metadata to requests so Dedicated/Private proxies can apply weighted eviction instead of binary drop.
Console displays current census snapshot, active credits, and predicted burn impact with a one-click revoke/extend action.
Runbook automation: on credit grant failures or policy violations the system opens an incident run (links in response).
Unit and integration tests cover credit accounting, expiry, and edge cases (clock skew, double-grant prevention).
design_decisions: Use a separate rolling job at the control plane (not on dataplane) to avoid adding latency to inference requests.
Census keying: endpoint_id + model_variant + region + tenant_bucket for accurate weighting.
Credit token model: immutable token minted at grant time with expiry and revocation flag to simplify enforcement in proxies.
Conservative default policy: only grant credits when global spare-error-budget > 2% and endpoint burn-rate > 1.5x baseline.
Fallthrough behavior: if proxies cannot honour weighted eviction, they must fallback to pre-configured circuit-breaker thresholds.
implementation_steps: Spec schema: define census metric payload and credit token format (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/621)
Control-plane job: implement rolling collector and aggregator with 1-minute cadence and 12-hour sliding retention
Orchestrator rules engine: implement grant/revoke, conflict resolution, and credit accounting
Proxy integration: add credit token enforcement path and weighted-eviction policy in dedicated proxy image
Console frontend: add 'SLI Census' panel, credit timeline, and one-click controls
E2E tests: simulate regional failover and verify credit lifecycle and request-level effects
Gradual rollout: canary to non-critical endpoints, telemetry gating, promote to critical after 2 weeks
open_questions: Should credit cost be charged to the endpoint's tenant or drawn from a global reserve by default?
How should quality regressions while on credit be surfaced to customers to avoid silent SLA violations?
What's the expected load and cardinality for census keys in very large customers (100k endpoints)? Need performance budget?
Should credits be composable (stacked) or single active credit per endpoint at a time?
recent_updates: 2025-02-11: Kickoff meeting with reliability, routing, and console teams. Agreed on 1-minute cadence and token model.
2025-02-18: Prototype aggregator implemented; measured memory cost for 1M keys in staging (PR linked).
2025-02-22: Design review feedback from Security: require signed credit tokens and audit logs (added to schema).
2025-02-25: CLI and API contract drafted; Marcus Li opened infra PR to add credit verification endpoint (github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/621).
2025-02-28: Integration test harness for simulating regional ejections is green in staging; observed expected reduction in manual overrides.
risks_mitigation: Risk: Over-granting credits could erode global error budget -> Mitigation: hard global reserve threshold and exponential backoff on repeated grants.
Risk: Proxies failing to enforce tokens -> Mitigation: fail-open only for non-critical endpoints and require audit annotation for any open behavior.
Risk: High cardinality causing control-plane pressure -> Mitigation: sampling tier and tenant_bucket aggregation for very high-cardinality customers.
Risk: Customer confusion -> Mitigation: console annotations and automated customer-facing emails when credits alter perceived quality.
